title: Far Worlds - A cozy exploration adventure with a tech stack that runs Three.js at native performance (using Vulkan/Metal/etc) on PC, Mac, Linux, Android, iOS, and soon consoles.
author: Braydo25
selftext:
Hey all!

I'm really excited to share a game I've been working on for the last 2 years. It's called Far Worlds. I took a lot of inspiration from games I love (Minecraft, Terraria & Stardew Valley) to create this co-op mmorpg-lite game where you can play solo, match up and go on adventures with other players, or go at it and play with friends.

In Far Worlds, you're an adventurer who comes across an old run down camp with a bit of mystery. Upon arrival a guide there notices you wandering at night and offers you to stay for the night. He suggests why not help him build the camp back up to its former glory in exchange for him keeping you safe and taking you out on adventures to gather materials, explore and more.

I built the game on a core explore, gather, return type of loop. Your camp is your home base, travellers come in over time and want to settle - you build beds, houses, etc for them to stay. They give you quests and also help build up the camp. There's camp projects that are sort of milestone goals that you gather materials for on your adventures to rebuild the camp.

As you rebuild, some more mystery plays out that I won't spoil, but that's the high level gist of the game.

It's in early alpha, but playable in browser, there's also a mobile app for Android/iOS that's early access you can find here: [https://farworlds.com/download](https://farworlds.com/download)

You can play in browser at [https://farworlds.com/play](https://farworlds.com/play)

This game is built on top of a game engine I developed back in 2024. We use Claude for a lot of supporting infrastructure and task automation now, test suites, and QoL work.

The renderer was rebuilt so while we build the game using three.js, it has a native under the hood renderer built with Rust/WGPU - as well as lightweight native wrappers for iOS, Android, Pc, Mac and Linux variations for the non-browser game. This lets us run native frame rates/performance on those devices. Mac/iOS runs Metal, PC/Android Vulkan, etc. Claude helped us dramatically on this front - we basically built a package that updates/pulls content from the web game service, and runs native with a singular codebase and native performance on the rednerer side unhindered by Three.js no matter where we ship.

  
We're thinking of open sourcing the stack to developers. This lets you use three.js and basically ship your game everywhere (Steam, app stores, will even compile to consoles with a bit more work). Let me know if you have any deeper questions on the stack!

  
Let me know what you think!
